title: A 30-second database blip became a 40-minute outage (retry storm)
intro: At 09:00 the inventory database had a 30-second failover, which is normal and expected. But the whole shop stayed down for 40 minutes afterwards, with inventory's pods pinned at 100% CPU long after the database was healthy again. The request path is frontend → checkout → inventory → db.

steps.prompt: Compare the request rate each layer received during the incident: query Prometheus for the per-service request rate (sum by service of rate over 1m of http_requests_total, services frontend, checkout, and inventory).
Users sent 1,000 req/s, but inventory received 27,000: 27x amplification. Check the retry policy on the VirtualService checkout in shop.
expected_commands: kubectl get virtualservice checkout -n shop -o yaml
kubectl get vs checkout -n shop -o yaml

steps.prompt: The mesh retries 3 times, and so do the app clients inside each service (3 layers × 3 tries = 27). Check the inventory VirtualService in shop too.
expected_commands: kubectl get virtualservice inventory -n shop -o yaml
kubectl get vs inventory -n shop -o yaml

steps.prompt: Stop the amplification now: apply the prepared VirtualService with retries limited to 1 attempt at the edge only, from vs-retries-fixed.yaml, in shop.
Confirm inventory's load dropped: rerun the per-service rate query.
steps.hint: Same query as the first step.

resolution: The database failover lasted 30 seconds, but every failed call was retried 3 times at each of 3 layers, so inventory received up to 27 requests for each user request. That load kept inventory overloaded, which caused more timeouts, which caused more retries: a self-sustaining retry storm that outlived its trigger by 40 minutes. Nothing was 'broken' after 09:01; the system was stuck in a metastable failure state it couldn't leave on its own. Fixes: retry at one layer only (usually the edge or the direct caller), with a small attempt count; use exponential backoff with jitter so retries don't arrive in synchronized waves; add retry budgets (for example, retries may be at most 10% of requests) as gRPC and Envoy support; and pair retries with circuit breaking (sre-tutorial-003), so a clearly failing dependency gets less traffic rather than more. Google's SRE book and AWS's Builders' Library both treat retry amplification as a top cause of large outages.
real_commands_used: promtool query instant sum by (service) rate
